title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction: Setting: A is an elliptic curve and P is (very probably) a smooth projective curve; 'P^E' is unclear in the image. Y = A × P is a surface. On A×A, Θ0 = Δ − A×(0) − (0)×A is the divisor giving the self-duality (principal polarization) of A: its restriction to {a}×A is (a)−(0). Pull it back to Θ = Θ0 × P, a divisor on A×A×P = A×Y. Let L be an invertible sheaf on Y (probably ample), with class c = cl(L). Let X be the projective closure of the line bundle V(L), i.e. the P^1-bundle P(L⊕O) over Y, a threefold. Let i: Y → X be the zero section; its normal bundle is L (or its dual, depending on convention, hence the remark about 'two conventions'). Set i' = id_A × i: A×Y → A×X and z = i'_*(cl Θ), a codimension-2 cycle on the 4-fold A×X. With s: A×X → A and t: A×Y → A the projections, the task is to compute s_*(z^2), a divisor class (0-cycle) on the curve A. The self-intersection formula gives z^2 = i'_*(Θ · i'^*i'_*Θ) = i'_*(Θ^2 · c'), where c' = i'^*i'_*(1) = c_1(normal bundle of i') = 1_A × c. Hence s_*(z^2) = t_*(Θ^2 · (1_A × c)). The page stops here. Completing it: Θ0^2 on A×A has degree −2. This uses Δ^2 = 0, (A×0)^2 = ((0)×A)^2 = 0, Δ·(A×0) = Δ·((0)×A) = 1 and (A×0)·((0)×A) = 1. So Θ^2 = Θ0^2 × P, and the degree of s_*(z^2) equals −2·deg(L|_{fibre P}), up to the normal-bundle sign convention. This is negative when L is ample on the fibres. Purpose: the fibres z_a = i_*(((a)−(0)) × P) form a family of cycles on X parametrized by A that are homologically trivial (indeed algebraically trivial). s_*(z^2) is the pull-back of the 'polarization' that intersection theory induces on such families. The example is a sign test for the expected definiteness of the intersection pairing on algebraically trivial cycles (a Hodge-index/Weil-positivity analogue). This is the kind of statement entering the standard conjectures and Weil-style positivity, and the sign check fixes the convention.
errors: Notation slip: 'z^2 = i'_*(clΘ)^2' should read (i'_*clΘ)^2 = i'_*(Θ·i'^*i'_*Θ) = i'_*(Θ^2·c'). The final formula is correct.
The sign of c' depends on whether V(L) is taken in the EGA convention (normal bundle L^∨) or the other one. The author flags 'deux conventions', so this is not an error but a pending sign.
The computation is unfinished: the value of s_*(z^2) is never written down.

ideas.what: Using the self-intersection formula i^*i_*(1) = c_1(N) to compute the square of a cycle pushed forward from a zero section into a projective line-bundle closure

Building a family of algebraically trivial codim-2 cycles on a threefold X parametrized by an elliptic curve, via the Poincaré-type divisor Δ−A×0−0×A, and computing s_*(z^2) to test the sign of the induced pairing
ideas.modern_name: sign test of the Hodge-index / positivity for algebraically trivial cycles (polarization on Albanese/intermediate Jacobian induced by correspondences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (positivity for curves), Grothendieck (standard conjectures, 1969); later Beilinson–Bloch height sign conventions
ideas.where_published: related in spirit to 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969), but this specific example is not there as far as known

deep.surprise_reason: A routine, unfinished sign check on a toy example: a P^1-bundle over (elliptic curve × curve), with a cycle family from the Poincaré divisor. It illustrates Grothendieck testing positivity conventions for the standard conjectures. Nothing here appears to be a new result absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Y^? → X^3' should be 'Y^2 → X^3' (superscripts denote dimensions: surface Y into threefold X).
'P courbe non[?] proj.[?] complète[?]' is likely 'P courbe non singulière projective complète' (or similar).
'ample[?]' in the line about L is uncertain; the image reads roughly 'faisceau inv. L ...'.

'c' = i'^*i'_*(1) = c^1 (faisceau normal pour i')' reads as c_1 of the normal sheaf for i'. And 'c étant le faisceau normal pour Y' should be read as 'c étant [la classe du] faisceau normal pour i: Y → X'.
